title: Themes
text:
theme() takes a preset and individual options. The presets follow ggplot2’s complete themes:







Preset
Look




vega
Vega-Lite’s defaults


gray (also grey, ggplot2)
gray panel with white grid lines, and ggplot2’s hue palette


bw
white panel with a dark border and light grid


linedraw
white panel with a black border and thin black grid lines


minimal
light grid, no border, and no axis lines


classic
axis lines and no grid


light
light gray border and grid


dark
dark background


void
no axes or grid



baseSize: scales every font size, with ggplot2’s proportions. Themes are written into the specification as Vega-Lite config, so HTML and static exports look the same.
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point()
    ->theme('gray', baseSize: 12);

The individual options are:

font, textColor, and baseSize
legendPosition (right, left, top, bottom, or none), legendDirection (horizontal or vertical), and legendTitle: false
background, panelBackground, and panelBorder
grid, gridColor, axisLine, and ticks
xLabelAngle and yLabelAngle, which turn axis labels anticlockwise as element_text(angle =) does
titleAnchor and padding
captionSize, captionColor, and captionAnchor, which style labs(caption:)

config: accepts raw Vega-Lite config, merged last. Calls without a preset build on the current theme.
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point()
    ->theme('minimal', legendPosition: 'bottom', font: 'Georgia, serif', config: ['axis' => ['labelColor' => '#666666']])
    ->labs(title: 'A minimal theme with the legend below');

A page can also choose a theme at render time. The vega-embed option theme accepts the vega-themes names, and phiz adds 'auto', which follows the reader’s light or dark mode preference:
$plot->embed(['theme' => 'auto']);

title: Scales, coordinates, and labels
text:
scaleX(), scaleY(), scaleColor(), scaleFill(), scaleSize(), scaleShape(), scaleOpacity(), and scaleLinetype() configure the scale and guide for one aesthetic. Successive calls for the same aesthetic merge.
Scale options are passed to the Vega-Lite scale:

type: linear, log, sqrt, pow, symlog, time, ordinal, quantile, quantize, or threshold
domain and range
scheme, a Vega color scheme such as viridis, blues, set2, or tableau10
values, a manual palette as a level-to-value map or a list in level order
zero, nice, reverse, clamp, base, exponent, domainMid, and padding

Guide options are passed to the axis or legend:

name, the title
breaks, the tick or legend values
format, a d3 number or time format
labels, a label formatter (below), a map from values to labels, a list of labels for breaks, or a Vega label expression
guide: false, which hides the axis or legend

use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::economics())
    ->aes(x: 'pop', y: 'pce')
    ->point(alpha: 0.4)
    ->scaleY(type: 'log', breaks: [500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000], name: 'Personal consumption ($bn, log scale)')
    ->scaleX(format: '.3s', name: 'Population (thousands)');

use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point(size: 40)
    ->scaleColor(values: ['f' => '#1B9E77', 'r' => '#7570B3', '4' => '#D95F02'], name: 'Drive');

Continuous position scales fit the data as in ggplot2: points and lines do not force the axis to include zero. Plots with bars, areas, histograms, or densities keep zero, since their lengths are measured from it. zero: true restores Vega-Lite’s default for a single scale.
The functions in Phiz\ include ggplot2’s shortcuts. Each returns a closure for the pipe operator or apply():







Function
Scale




scale_x_log10(), scale_x_sqrt(), scale_x_reverse(), scale_x_date()
transformed and date position scales


scale_x_discrete(limits:, labels:)
discrete positions: limits orders and subsets the levels, labels renames them


scale_color_manual(values)
a level-to-color map, or colors in level order


scale_color_brewer(palette), scale_color_distiller(), scale_color_fermenter()
ColorBrewer palettes for discrete, continuous, and binned data


scale_color_viridis_d(), _c(), _b()
viridis with option (A magma to E cividis, H turbo), begin, end, and direction


scale_color_gradient(), scale_color_gradient2(), scale_color_gradientn()
two-color, diverging, and many-color gradients


scale_color_hue(h:, c:, l:, hStart:, direction:)
ggplot2’s hue palette with its options


scale_color_grey(start:, end:)
grays, as grey.colors()


scale_color_identity()
the data values are the colors, with no legend



Each scale_color_*() has a scale_fill_*() twin. The hue and grey palettes are computed for the number of levels in the data.


The label functions follow the scales package. Pass one as labels:.



Function
0.256
12500




label_percent()
25.6%
1250000%


label_comma()
0.256
12,500


label_dollar()
$0.256
$12,500


label_number(accuracy: 0.1, suffix: ' kg')
0.3 kg
12,500.0 kg


label_scientific()
2.56e-1
1.25e+4


label_date('%b %Y')
for dates




accuracy rounds (0.01 keeps two decimals, and the default trims trailing zeros), scale multiplies first, and prefix and suffix wrap the number. label_dollar(scale: 0.001, suffix: 'k') writes 12500 as $12.5k.
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

use function Phiz\guide_axis;
use function Phiz\label_percent;
use function Phiz\scale_fill_viridis_d;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'class', fill: 'drv')
    ->bar(position: 'fill')
    ->scaleY(labels: label_percent(), name: 'Share of cars')
    ->apply(scale_fill_viridis_d(begin: 0.2, end: 0.8))
    ->guides(x: guide_axis(angle: 45))
    ->labs(x: null, fill: 'Drive');




guides() sets the axis or legend for each aesthetic, as ggplot2’s guides() does. 'none' hides one. guide_axis(angle:) turns axis labels, guide_legend(title:, ncol:, direction:) arranges a legend, and guide_colorbar(barwidth:, barheight:) sizes a color bar. Any other Vega-Lite axis or legend property can be passed as a named argument.
guide_axis(cap: true) draws the axis line only from the first break to the last, as ggplot2’s guide_axis(cap = "both") does. With a padded domain, such as scaleX(domain: [-4, 104], breaks: [0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100]), the line stops at 0 and 100 and stands apart from the panel corners. It needs breaks or a domain. Faceted plots do not support it, because the line would be drawn in every panel.
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

use function Phiz\scale_color_grey;
use function Phiz\scale_x_discrete;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'drv', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->boxplot()
    ->apply(scale_x_discrete(limits: ['f', 'r', '4'], labels: ['f' => 'Front', 'r' => 'Rear', '4' => '4WD']))
    ->apply(scale_color_grey())
    ->guides(color: 'none')
    ->labs(x: 'Drive', y: 'Highway mpg')
    ->theme('bw');

title: Scales, coordinates, and labels
Scales, coordinates, and labels
text:
Labels
labs() sets the title, subtitle, caption, and the title for any aesthetic. A null title removes it. Titles for position aesthetics apply to everything drawn on that axis, including ranges and reference lines. A facet field’s name sets its panel header title.
$plot->labs(title: 'Fuel economy', subtitle: 'EPA data, 1999 and 2008', x: 'Displacement (L)', y: 'Highway mpg', color: 'Drive');
The caption is placed below the plot, under the axis titles. By default it is right-aligned and smaller than the axis titles, as in ggplot2. theme(captionSize:, captionColor:, captionAnchor:) changes its size, color, and alignment (start, middle, or end). Vega-Lite gives each view one title. A plot with both a title and a caption is therefore emitted as a vconcat that holds the single view, with the title on the outside and the caption on the view. Vega-Lite does not apply autosize fit to a vconcat. In such a plot, size() sets the plot area alone, and the titles, axes, and caption are added around it. A caption without a title keeps the exact size under autosize fit.

text: This reference is generated from the public signatures and docblocks in src/. Every method that adds or changes something returns a new Plot, and the plot it was called on is unchanged.

title: API reference
text:
Exceptions

InvalidArgumentException for input phiz cannot use, such as an unknown aesthetic, scale type, theme, or legend position, a geom without an aesthetic it needs, data that is neither rows nor columns, or a plot with no layers. The message names the problem.
Phiz\Exceptions\VlConvertNotFound when static export cannot find the vl-convert binary.
Phiz\Exceptions\ExportFailed when vl-convert fails, times out, or writes nothing, or when a file cannot be written.

Both export exceptions implement Phiz\Exceptions\PhizException.

text:
Plot

Construction
Plot::of(mixed $data = null, Aes|array|null $aes = null): Plot
A plot of rows, columns, a phibble Table, a Laravel Collection, or Data::url(…), with optional mappings.


Mappings and data
->aes(mixed ...$mappings): Plot
Adds plot-wide aesthetic mappings: x, y, color, fill, size, shape, alpha, group, tooltip, label, …
->data(mixed $data): Plot


Geoms
->point(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, int|float|null $alpha = null, int|float|null $size = null, ?string $color = null, ?string $fill = null, string|int|null $shape = null, array|int|float|bool|null $jitter = null, ?string $position = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Scatterplot points. jitter: true (or a width, or [width, height]) displaces them randomly.
->jitter(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, int|float|null $width = null, int|float $height = 0, int|float|null $alpha = null, int|float|null $size = null, ?string $color = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Points jittered by up to width/height (fraction of a band on discrete axes, data units otherwise).
->line(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, int|float|null $alpha = null, int|float|null $linewidth = null, ?string $color = null, array|string|null $linetype = null, ?int $downsample = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Lines connecting points in order of x. downsample: n keeps about n points per group (LTTB), in PHP.
->path(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, int|float|null $alpha = null, int|float|null $linewidth = null, ?string $color = null, array|string|null $linetype = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Lines connecting points in data order.
->step(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, string $direction = 'hv', int|float|null $linewidth = null, ?string $color = null, array|string|null $linetype = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Stairsteps: direction ‘hv’ (horizontal first), ‘vh’, or ‘mid’.
->area(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, string $position = 'stack', int|float|null $alpha = null, ?string $fill = null, ?string $color = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Areas from zero, stacked by fill (position: stack, fill, identity).
->ribbon(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, int|float|null $alpha = null, ?string $fill = null, ?string $color = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
A band between ymin and ymax (or xmin and xmax).
->bar(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, string $position = 'stack', int|float|null $width = null, int|float|null $alpha = null, ?string $fill = null, ?string $color = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Bars of counts of x (or y), or of the y values when y is mapped. position: stack, dodge, fill, identity.
->col(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, string $position = 'stack', int|float|null $width = null, int|float|null $alpha = null, ?string $fill = null, ?string $color = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Bars whose heights are the y values.
->histogram(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, ?int $bins = null, int|float|null $binwidth = null, int|float|null $boundary = null, string $position = 'stack', bool $density = false, string $compute = 'auto', int|float|null $alpha = null, ?string $fill = null, ?string $color = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Binned counts of x: bins (a maximum; Vega-Lite picks nice boundaries) or binwidth. density: true scales to unit area. compute: ‘server’ bins in PHP (exactly bins equal-width bins), ‘browser’ in Vega-Lite, and ‘auto’ (the default) in PHP above Config::$serverRows rows.
->freqpoly(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, ?int $bins = null, int|float|null $binwidth = null, int|float|null $linewidth = null, ?string $color = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Frequency polygons: binned counts drawn as lines.
->density(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, int|float|null $bw = null, int|float|null $adjust = null, ?array $extent = null, ?int $n = null, bool $counts = false, ?string $position = null, int|float|null $alpha = null, ?string $fill = null, ?string $color = null, int|float|null $linewidth = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Kernel density of x per group (Vega-Lite’s density transform). bw sets the bandwidth; adjust multiplies it (from R’s bw.nrd0 when bw is unset); counts: true scales to counts.
->boxplot(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, int|float $coef = 1.5, bool $outliers = true, int|float|null $width = null, int|float|null $alpha = null, ?string $fill = null, ?string $color = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot

Violins: the kernel density of y per level of a discrete x. bw sets the bandwidth, adjust multiplies R’s bw.nrd0, and width is the widest violin’s share of its band. They layer with boxplot() and jitter().

Error bars from ymin to ymax (or xmin to xmax) with end ticks; width is the tick length in pixels.

Vertical (or horizontal) lines from ymin to ymax.

A point at y on a line from ymin to ymax: the coefficient-plot geom. position: ‘dodge’ sets groups side by side.

Horizontal reference lines at fixed values, or at a mapped yintercept field when yintercept is null.

Vertical reference lines at fixed values, or at a mapped xintercept field.

Line segments from (x, y) to (xend, yend).

->tile(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, ?string $color = null, int|float|null $alpha = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot

Alias of tile().
->rect(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, ?string $fill = null, ?string $color = null, int|float|null $alpha = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot

->hex(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, int $bins = 30, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Hexagonal bins counted in PHP, as ggplot2’s geom_hex: bins hexagons across the x range.
->smooth(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, string $method = 'loess', ?bool $se = null, float $level = 0.95, float $span = 0.75, int $order = 3, int $n = 80, ?string $color = null, ?string $fill = null, int|float|null $linewidth = null, array|string|null $linetype = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
A fitted curve per group. method: loess (span sets the bandwidth), lm, poly (order), quad, log, exp, pow. With se (the default for lm, quad and poly with inline data) the fit and a level confidence band are computed in PHP; otherwise Vega-Lite fits the curve and no band is drawn.
->density2d(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, ?int $bins = null, int|float|null $binwidth = null, ?array $breaks = null, array|int|float|null $h = null, int|float $adjust = 1, int $n = 100, string $contourVar = 'density', ?string $color = null, int|float|null $linewidth = null, int|float|null $alpha = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Contour lines of a 2D kernel density of x and y, as ggplot2’s geom_density_2d (MASS::kde2d on an n × n grid). h sets the bandwidths ([x, y] or one for both; default MASS::bandwidth.nrd), adjust multiplies them, and bins, binwidth, or breaks set the levels (default pretty(range, 10)). contourVar: density, ndensity (scaled to a maximum of 1 per group), or count. aes(color: ‘level’) colors lines by their level.
->density2dFilled(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, ?int $bins = null, int|float|null $binwidth = null, ?array $breaks = null, array|int|float|null $h = null, int|float $adjust = 1, int $n = 100, string $contourVar = 'density', int|float|null $alpha = null, ?string $color = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Filled bands of a 2D kernel density between consecutive breaks, as ggplot2’s geom_density_2d_filled.
->contour(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, ?int $bins = null, int|float|null $binwidth = null, ?array $breaks = null, ?string $color = null, int|float|null $linewidth = null, int|float|null $alpha = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Contour lines of z over a regular grid of x and y, as ggplot2’s geom_contour; bins, binwidth, or breaks.
->contourFilled(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, ?int $bins = null, int|float|null $binwidth = null, ?array $breaks = null, int|float|null $alpha = null, ?string $color = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Filled contour bands of z over a regular grid, as ggplot2’s geom_contour_filled.
->polygon(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, ?string $fill = null, ?string $color = null, int|float|null $alpha = null, int|float|null $linewidth = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Filled polygons through the points in data order, one per group (or fill level). Rows with null x and y start a new ring within a group; a ring drawn in the opposite direction cuts a hole.
->summary(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, Closure|string|null $funData = null, Closure|string|null $fun = null, Closure|string|null $funMin = null, Closure|string|null $funMax = null, array $funArgs = [], ?string $geom = null, ?string $position = null, int|float|null $width = null, ?string $color = null, int|float|null $size = null, int|float|null $linewidth = null, int|float|null $alpha = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Summaries of y at each x, drawn with geom (pointrange by default), as ggplot2’s stat_summary. funData: mean_se (the default), mean_cl_normal, mean_sdl, median_hilow, or a callable returning [y, ymin, ymax]. fun, funMin, and funMax: mean, median, min, max, sum, sd, n, or callables of the group’s values. funArgs passes mult or conf. geom: pointrange, errorbar, linerange, crossbar, point, line, col, area, or ribbon.
->crossbar(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, int|float|null $width = null, ?string $position = null, ?string $color = null, ?string $fill = null, int|float|null $linewidth = null, int|float|null $alpha = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
A box from ymin to ymax with a line at y, as ggplot2’s geom_crossbar; width is a share of the band.
->ellipse(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, string $type = 't', float $level = 0.95, int $segments = 51, string $geom = 'path', ?string $color = null, ?string $fill = null, int|float|null $linewidth = null, array|string|null $linetype = null, int|float|null $alpha = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Confidence ellipses per group, as ggplot2’s stat_ellipse: type ‘t’ (a robust multivariate t fit), ‘norm’, or ‘euclid’ (a circle of radius level), at level. geom: ‘polygon’ fills them.
->count(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, ?string $color = null, int|float|null $alpha = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Points sized by how many rows share each x and y, as ggplot2’s geom_count.
->annotate(string $geom, mixed $x = null, mixed $y = null, mixed $xmin = null, mixed $xmax = null, mixed $ymin = null, mixed $ymax = null, mixed $xend = null, mixed $yend = null, mixed $label = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
A layer of fixed values rather than data, as ggplot2’s annotate(): annotate(‘text’, x: 4, y: 40, label: ‘Note’), annotate(‘rect’, xmin: 2, xmax: 3, ymin: -INF …). Positions are numbers, dates, or levels, or lists of them for several marks. Annotations ignore the plot’s mappings and appear in every facet panel. geom: text, label, point, segment, rect, pointrange, linerange, errorbar, crossbar, or rule.
->curve(callable $fn, int|float $from, int|float $to, int $n = 101, Aes|array|null $aes = null, ?string $color = null, array|string|null $linetype = null, int|float|null $linewidth = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
A function of x drawn from from to to, as ggplot2’s geom_function.
->rug(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, ?string $sides = null, int $length = 8, ?string $color = null, int|float|null $alpha = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Marginal ticks: sides ‘b’ (bottom, for x), ‘l’ (left, for y), or ‘bl’; length in pixels.
->ecdf(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, ?string $color = null, int|float|null $linewidth = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Empirical cumulative distribution of x per group.
->qq(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, ?string $color = null, int|float|null $size = null, int|float|null $alpha = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Normal quantile-quantile points of the sample aesthetic.
->qqLine(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, ?string $color = null, array|string|null $linetype = null, int|float|null $linewidth = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
The QQ reference line through the sample’s quartiles.
->arc(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, int|float|null $innerRadius = null, ?string $color = null, bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Pie (or donut, with innerRadius in pixels) slices sized by theta, or counts of fill.
->pie(Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, int|float|null $innerRadius = null, mixed ...$style): Plot
Alias of arc().
->layer(array $spec): Plot
A raw Vega-Lite layer, used as given.
->geom(string $geom, Aes|array|null $aes = null, mixed $data = null, array $params = [], array $style = [], bool $inheritAes = true, array|string|null $filter = null, array $raw = []): Plot
Adds a geom by name with options: the generic form behind the geom methods.


Scales
->scale(string $aesthetic, mixed ...$options): Plot
Sets the scale for an aesthetic; see Scale::make() for the options.
->scaleX(mixed ...$options): Plot
x scale: type (linear, log, sqrt, time, …), domain, range, zero, nice, reverse, name, breaks, labels, format.
->scaleY(mixed ...$options): Plot
->scaleColor(mixed ...$options): Plot
Color scale: scheme (‘viridis’, ‘blues’, ‘category10’, …), range, values (manual palette), domainMid, …
->scaleFill(mixed ...$options): Plot
->scaleSize(mixed ...$options): Plot
->scaleShape(mixed ...$options): Plot
->scaleOpacity(mixed ...$options): Plot
->scaleLinetype(mixed ...$options): Plot
->guides(mixed ...$guides): Plot
Guides per aesthetic, as ggplot2’s guides(): ‘none’ or false hides one, and an array sets axis or legend properties (see guide_legend(), guide_colorbar(), and guide_axis()).
->xlim(string|int|float $min, string|int|float $max): Plot
Fixes the x domain. Unlike ggplot2’s xlim(), data outside it is clipped rather than dropped.
->ylim(string|int|float $min, string|int|float $max): Plot


Coordinates and facets
->coordFlip(bool $flip = true): Plot
Swaps the x and y channels, so mappings stay as written while the plot turns sideways.
->coordPolar(string $theta = 'x', float $start = 0.0, int $direction = 1, int|float $innerRadius = 0): Plot
Polar coordinates for bar() and col() layers, as ggplot2’s coord_polar. theta: ‘y’ turns stacked bars into a pie (map x to a constant, or leave it out; innerRadius in pixels makes a donut), and ‘x’ turns bars over a discrete x into a rose of equal angles with radius y. start rotates the first slice clockwise from twelve o’clock, in radians; direction -1 runs anticlockwise.
->coordFixed(int|float $ratio = 1): Plot
A fixed aspect ratio, as ggplot2’s coord_fixed: one unit of y takes ratio times the length of one unit of x. The panel’s height follows from the width (300 pixels unless set) and the data ranges, which are kept exact.
->coordCartesian(?array $xlim = null, ?array $ylim = null): Plot
Zooms to fixed domains, clipping marks outside them.
->facetWrap(array|string $facets, ?int $ncol = null, ?int $nrow = null, string $scales = 'fixed', array|string $labeller = 'value', array $header = []): Plot
Small multiples wrapped into rows. scales: fixed, free, free_x, free_y. With several fields the panels are their combinations. labeller: ‘both’ labels panels “field: value”, as ggplot2’s label_both.
->facetGrid(?string $rows = null, ?string $cols = null, string $scales = 'fixed', array|string $labeller = 'value', array $header = []): Plot
A grid of panels by rows and/or cols fields.


Labels, theme, size
->labs(mixed ...$labels): Plot
Titles: title, subtitle, caption, and one per aesthetic (x, y, color, fill, size, shape, …). A facet field’s name sets its panel header title. Null removes a title. The caption sits below the plot; theme() styles it.
->title(?string $title, ?string $subtitle = null): Plot
->theme(?string $preset = null, int|float|null $baseSize = null, ?string $font = null, ?string $legendPosition = null, ?string $background = null, ?string $panelBackground = null, ?string $panelBorder = null, ?bool $grid = null, ?string $titleAnchor = null, int|float|null $padding = null, int|float|null $xLabelAngle = null, int|float|null $yLabelAngle = null, ?string $legendDirection = null, ?bool $legendTitle = null, ?bool $axisLine = null, ?bool $ticks = null, ?string $gridColor = null, ?string $textColor = null, int|float|null $captionSize = null, ?string $captionColor = null, ?string $captionAnchor = null, array $config = []): Plot
A theme preset (gray, bw, linedraw, minimal, classic, light, dark, void, vega) and/or individual options; config is raw Vega-Lite config merged last. Successive calls build on each other. xLabelAngle and yLabelAngle turn axis labels anticlockwise, as element_text(angle =); legendTitle: false, axisLine, and ticks switch those parts. captionSize, captionColor, and captionAnchor (start, middle, or end) style labs(caption:).
->size(string|int|null $width = null, string|int|null $height = null): Plot
Width and height in pixels (per panel when faceted); ‘container’ fills the parent element’s width.
->width(string|int $width): Plot
->height(string|int $height): Plot
->description(string $description): Plot


Interaction
->tooltip(array|string|bool $fields = true): Plot
Tooltips on every layer: true shows the encoded fields, a list shows those fields.
->interactive(array $encodings = [0 => 'x',1 => 'y'], string $name = 'zoom'): Plot
Pan and zoom by dragging and scrolling (scales bound to an interval selection).
->brush(string $name = 'brush', array $encodings = [0 => 'x'], ?string $unselected = '#cccccc', string $channel = 'color'): Plot
A drag-to-select interval named $name. Unselected marks of the first layer turn $unselected; other layers can react with filter: [‘param’ => $name], and linked plots in a composition share it.
->highlight(string $aesthetic = 'color', string $name = 'highlight', ?string $bind = 'legend', float $opacity = 0.15): Plot
Click legend entries (or marks, with bind: null) to highlight their group; others fade to $opacity.
->slider(string $name, int|float $min, int|float $max, int|float|null $step = null, int|float|null $value = null, ?string $label = null): Plot
A slider bound to a parameter; use expr($name) in geoms or a filter to react to it.
->dropdown(string $name, array $options, mixed $value = null, ?string $label = null): Plot
A dropdown bound to a parameter.
->param(string $name, mixed $value = null, ?array $bind = null, ?string $expr = null): Plot
A Vega-Lite parameter: a value, optionally bound to an input, or an expr.
->select(array $param): Plot
A raw selection parameter, attached to the first layer.


Escape hatches
->transform(array ...$transforms): Plot
Vega-Lite transforms applied to the data before every layer.
->raw(array $spec): Plot
Raw Vega-Lite merged into the top-level spec last (nested objects merge; lists and scalars replace).
->apply(callable ...$fns): Plot
Applies a function to the plot: pipe-friendly composition of reusable plot fragments.
->toArray(): array
->toSpec(): array

title: API reference
text:
Functions
Most functions in the Phiz\ namespace return a closure that applies the method of the same name, for the pipe operator and apply(). They take the same arguments as that method.

aes(mixed ...$mappings): Aes: Aesthetic mappings: aes(x: ‘displ’, y: ‘hwy’, color: ‘class’).
ggplot(mixed $data = null, Aes|array|null $mapping = null): Plot: A plot of data with optional mappings.
field(string $name, ?string $type = null, mixed ...$properties): Field: A field with an explicit type or other Vega-Lite field-definition properties.
factor(string $name, ?array $levels = null): Field: A field treated as discrete categories, like R’s factor(cyl). Levels set the order.
calc(string $expression, string $as, ?string $type = null): Field: A field computed from a Vega expression: calc(‘datum.hwy - datum.cty’, as: ‘gap’).
expr(string $expression): Expr: A Vega expression, such as a slider parameter’s name.

->isInline(): bool

What the binning helpers read: the table, the columns, or the rows.

A field’s values, JSON-safe, read from the table or columns without building rows.

The Vega-Lite measurement type of a field: quantitative when every non-null value is a number, temporal when every value is an ISO date string, nominal otherwise. Null for non-inline data or an all-null column.

Distinct non-null values of a field in first-seen order.

The vl-convert binary path, or null when none is found.
Export::available(): bool

PNG bytes; scale multiplies the pixel size (2 for high-DPI screens), ppi sets the embedded resolution.
->jpeg(Chart|array $chart, float $scale = 2.0, ?int $quality = null): string

The compiled Vega (not Vega-Lite) spec.

Html

The container element for a chart.

A self-contained fragment: the container plus script tags (null assets means the pinned CDN copies).
Html::page(Chart|array|null $chart, ?string $title = null, array $options = [], ?Assets $assets = null, string $body = ''): string
Html::attributes(array $attributes): string


Bin
Bin::histogram(mixed $source, string $x, int $bins = 30, int|float|null $binwidth = null, int|float|null $boundary = null, ?array $limits = null, array $groups = []): array
Equal-width bins of x: rows with x0, x1, count, and density (count / (n * width)), per group.
Bin::grid(mixed $source, string $x, string $y, array|int $bins = 30, ?array $xlim = null, ?array $ylim = null, array $groups = []): array
Counts in a grid of x-by-y rectangles: rows with x_start, x_end, y_start, y_end (named after the fields) and count. Empty cells are omitted.
Bin::hex(mixed $source, string $x, string $y, int $bins = 30, ?array $xlim = null, ?array $ylim = null, float $aspect = 1.0, array $groups = []): array
Counts in a hexagonal grid, as ggplot2’s geom_hex: rows with the hexagon centers (under the x and y names) and count. bins hexagons span the x range; aspect (height / width of the panel in pixels) keeps them regular on screen.
Bin::lttb(array $rows, string $x, string $y, int $threshold = 1000, array $groups = []): array
Downsamples a line to about $threshold points with Largest-Triangle-Three-Buckets, which keeps the visual shape (peaks and troughs). Rows are sorted by x; groups are downsampled separately.
Bin::sample(mixed $source, int $n, int $seed = 1): array
A uniform random sample of n rows (reservoir sampling, one pass), reproducible with a seed.
Bin::range(mixed $source, string $field): array
The [min, max] of a numeric field, padded when every value is equal.
Bin::values(mixed $source, array $fields): Generator
The values of the named fields, one list per record.

title: Laravel and Livewire
text:
phiz’s Laravel service provider is discovered automatically. It registers the <x-phiz> Blade component and the @phizScripts directive. Without Laravel, the same classes are never loaded.
The component’s tests run on Laravel 12 through Orchestra Testbench 10. The Livewire behavior below is not covered by the test suite, and phiz does not depend on Livewire.

title: Laravel and Livewire
text:
Blade
<x-phiz :plot="$plot" class="h-80" />
The component accepts a Plot, a Compose, a specification array, or specification JSON. :options passes vega-embed options, merged over config('phiz.embed_options'). Other attributes go to the container element.
The first <x-phiz> on a page adds the script tags. To place them yourself, put @phizScripts in the layout.

title: phiz
text:
phiz draws charts from PHP data. A chart is described in parts: the data, a mapping from columns to visual properties such as position, color, and size, and one or more layers of marks such as points, lines, or bars. Scales, facets, labels, and themes adjust the result. This way of describing charts comes from R’s ggplot2, but the pages here do not assume you know it.
phiz compiles the description to a Vega-Lite specification, a JSON document that describes the chart. The browser draws the specification with vega-embed, and the vl-convert command-line tool renders it to SVG, PNG, or PDF. No JavaScript is written by hand.
Each chart in these pages is drawn from the code shown with it.

title: phiz
text:
Install
composer require phpstats/phiz
phiz supports PHP 8.3, 8.4, and 8.5, and CI tests all three. Examples written with the pipe operator |> need PHP 8.5. Each one also has a method-chain version for PHP 8.3 and 8.4.
phiz has no required dependencies beyond PHP. These are optional:

the vl-convert binary, for SVG, PNG, and PDF export (Rendering)
Laravel, for the <x-phiz> Blade component, whose service provider is discovered automatically (Laravel and Livewire)
phit, for predictions from formula fits in the statistics helpers (Statistics)

Get started builds a first chart and saves it.

title: phiz
text:
What phiz covers

An immutable Plot builder with fluent methods, and ggplot2-style functions for PHP’s pipe operator.
More than 40 geoms, including points, lines, areas, bars, histograms, densities, boxplots, violins, intervals, reference lines, text, heatmaps, hexagonal bins, smoothers, 2D densities and contours, QQ plots, and arcs.
Scales, label formatters, guides, coordinate flips, limits, polar and fixed coordinates, facets, compositions, labels, captions, and themes modeled on ggplot2’s complete themes.
Tooltips, pan and zoom, brushing, legend highlighting, sliders, and linked views, expressed as Vega-Lite parameters.
Statistical plots from phit model results and CmdStanPHP draws: coefficient plots, regression diagnostics, predicted values with confidence bands, marginal means, random effects, and posterior intervals.
HTML output, static export, and the <x-phiz> Blade component, which redraws when a Livewire component updates.

title: phiz
text:
The phpstats family
phiz is the visualization package of the phpstats family. phit fits models, phibble provides data frames, phplyr provides dplyr-style functions, and CmdStanPHP runs Stan. phiz depends on none of them, and plots their tables and results directly.

Output
A plot compiles to a Vega-Lite specification on demand.
$plot->toArray();        // the specification as a PHP array

title: Gallery
text: Each chart below is drawn from the code under it. The code uses the bundled datasets, loaded as $mpg = Datasets::mpg(), $mtcars = Datasets::mtcars(), $economics = Datasets::economics(), and $faithful = Datasets::faithful(). The statistics examples use a linear model fit and posterior draws defined at the top of examples/catalog.php, which holds every example.

title: Gallery
text:
Basics

Scatterplot
Points with a color mapping.

Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'class')
    ->point()
    ->labs(x: 'Engine displacement (L)', y: 'Highway mpg', color: 'Class');


Linear fit with confidence band
lm fits are computed in PHP, with a 95% band, per group.

Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point(alpha: 0.5)
    ->smooth(method: 'lm')
    ->labs(title: 'Bigger engines, fewer miles', x: 'Displacement (L)', y: 'Highway mpg', color: 'Drive');


With ggplot2-style functions
ggplot2-style functions compose with apply(), or with the pipe operator on PHP 8.5.

ggplot($mpg, aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy'))->apply(
        geom_point(alpha: 0.4),
        geom_smooth(span: 0.5),
        labs(title: 'Loess smooth', x: 'Displacement (L)', y: 'Highway mpg'),
        theme_minimal(),
    );


Time series
ISO dates are read as temporal fields.

Plot::of($economics)
    ->aes(x: 'date', y: 'unemploy')
    ->line(color: '#1F77B4')
    ->labs(title: 'US unemployment', x: null, y: 'Unemployed (thousands)');


Stacked area
Areas stack by fill.

Plot::of(array_merge(...array_map(fn ($r) => [
        ['date' => $r['date'], 'series' => 'Unemployed', 'value' => $r['unemploy']],
        ['date' => $r['date'], 'series' => 'Median weeks unemployed (x1000)', 'value' => $r['uempmed'] * 1000],
    ], array_slice($economics, -120))))
        ->aes(x: 'date', y: 'value', fill: 'series')
        ->area(alpha: 0.8)
        ->theme(legendPosition: 'bottom');


Labels
Text labels with nudges.

Plot::of(array_slice($mtcars, 0, 12))
    ->aes(x: 'wt', y: 'mpg', label: 'model')
    ->point()
    ->text(nudgeY: 8, size: 9)
    ->labs(x: 'Weight (1000 lbs)', y: 'mpg');

title: Gallery
text:
Distributions

Histogram
Binned counts; bins sets the maximum number of bins.

Plot::of($faithful)
    ->aes(x: 'waiting')
    ->histogram(bins: 30, fill: '#4C78A8')
    ->labs(x: 'Minutes between eruptions', y: 'Count');


Histogram with density
density: true scales bars to unit area, so a KDE overlays.

Plot::of($faithful)
    ->aes(x: 'eruptions')
    ->histogram(binwidth: 0.25, density: true, fill: '#DDDDDD', color: '#999999')
    ->density(color: '#D62728', linewidth: 2)
    ->labs(x: 'Eruption length (minutes)');


Density by group
Kernel densities per group with Vega-Lite’s density transform.

Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'hwy', fill: 'drv')
    ->density(alpha: 0.4)
    ->labs(x: 'Highway mpg', fill: 'Drive');


Boxplots
Tukey boxplots, flipped for readable labels.

Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'class', y: 'hwy', fill: 'class')
    ->boxplot()
    ->coordFlip()
    ->scaleFill(guide: false)
    ->labs(x: null, y: 'Highway mpg');


Violins with boxplots
Densities per level, layered with boxplots, in ggplot2’s gray theme and hue palette.

Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'class', y: 'hwy', fill: 'class')
    ->violin(alpha: 0.6)
    ->boxplot(width: 8, outliers: false)
    ->scaleFill(guide: false)
    ->theme('gray')
    ->labs(x: null, y: 'Highway mpg');


Jittered strip plot
Points spread within each band.

Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: factor('cyl'), y: 'hwy', color: factor('cyl'))
    ->jitter(width: 0.3, alpha: 0.6)
    ->labs(x: 'Cylinders', y: 'Highway mpg')
    ->scaleColor(guide: false);


Empirical CDF
Cumulative distributions per group.

Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'cty', color: 'drv')
    ->ecdf()
    ->labs(x: 'City mpg', y: 'Proportion ≤ x', color: 'Drive');


QQ plot
Sample quantiles against normal quantiles, with the quartile line.

Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(sample: 'hwy')
    ->qq(alpha: 0.6)
    ->qqLine(color: '#D62728');


2D density
Filled density bands from MASS::kde2d, computed in PHP, with the points on top.

Plot::of($faithful)
    ->aes(x: 'eruptions', y: 'waiting')
    ->density2dFilled()
    ->point(size: 6, color: 'white', alpha: 0.5)
    ->labs(x: 'Eruption (minutes)', y: 'Waiting (minutes)', fill: 'density');


Confidence ellipses
stat_ellipse: robust t ellipses per group.

Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point(alpha: 0.5)
    ->ellipse()
    ->labs(x: 'Displacement (L)', y: 'Highway mpg', color: 'Drive');

title: Gallery
text:
Counts

Bar chart of counts
bar() counts rows when y is unmapped.

Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'class')
    ->bar(fill: '#4C78A8')
    ->labs(x: null, y: 'Cars');


Dodged bars
Groups side by side.

Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'class', fill: 'drv')
    ->bar(position: 'dodge')
    ->labs(x: null, y: 'Cars', fill: 'Drive');


Proportions
position: fill stacks to 100%.

Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'class', fill: 'drv')
    ->bar(position: 'fill')
    ->scaleY(format: '%')
    ->labs(x: null, y: 'Share of cars', fill: 'Drive');


Bars of values
col() draws the y values, here an aggregate.

Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'manufacturer', y: 'mean(hwy)')
    ->col(fill: '#72B7B2')
    ->coordFlip()
    ->labs(x: null, y: 'Mean highway mpg');


Heatmap
Tiles filled by an aggregate.

Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'class', y: factor('cyl'), fill: 'mean(hwy)')
    ->tile(color: 'white')
    ->scaleFill(scheme: 'viridis')
    ->labs(x: null, y: 'Cylinders', fill: 'Mean hwy');


2D histogram
Counts in x-by-y bins.

Plot::of($faithful)
    ->aes(x: 'eruptions', y: 'waiting')
    ->bin2d(bins: 20)
    ->scaleFill(scheme: 'blues');


Donut
Arcs sized by counts.

Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(fill: 'drv')
    ->pie(innerRadius: 50)
    ->labs(fill: 'Drive');


Polar bars
coordPolar() turns bars into a rose.

Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'class', fill: 'class')
    ->bar()
    ->coordPolar()
    ->labs(fill: null);


Annotations
annotate() adds shaded ranges, segments, and text.

Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'cty', y: 'hwy')
    ->annotate('rect', xmin: 15, xmax: 20, ymin: -INF, ymax: INF, fill: 'orange', alpha: 0.2)
    ->count(alpha: 0.6)
    ->annotate('text', x: 30, y: 23, label: 'Most efficient', color: '#D62728')
    ->labs(x: 'City mpg', y: 'Highway mpg');

title: Gallery
text:
Facets

Small multiples
facetWrap with a fitted line in every panel.

Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy')
    ->point(alpha: 0.5)
    ->smooth(method: 'lm')
    ->facetWrap('class', ncol: 4)
    ->size(150, 120);


Grid of panels
Rows by drive, columns by year.

Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'cty', y: 'hwy')
    ->point(alpha: 0.5)
    ->abline(0, 1, linetype: 'dashed', color: '#888888')
    ->facetGrid(rows: 'drv', cols: 'year')
    ->size(200, 120);


Side by side
Compose::beside lays plots out like patchwork.

Compose::beside(
        Plot::of($faithful)->aes(x: 'eruptions', y: 'waiting')->point(alpha: 0.5)->size(260, 220),
        Plot::of($faithful)->aes(x: 'waiting')->histogram(bins: 20)->coordFlip()->size(120, 220),
    )->title('Old Faithful');

title: Gallery
text:
Scales and themes

Log scale
scaleX(type: log) with chosen breaks.

Plot::of($economics)
    ->aes(x: 'pce', y: 'psavert')
    ->point(alpha: 0.4)
    ->scaleX(type: 'log', breaks: [500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000], name: 'Personal consumption ($bn, log)')
    ->labs(y: 'Savings rate (%)');


Manual colors
A level => color map.

Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point()

title: Data and fields
text:
Field types
Vega-Lite needs a measurement type for every mapped field. phiz infers it from inline data:

quantitative, when every non-null value is an integer or a float
temporal, when every value is an ISO date or date-time string
nominal, otherwise

A numeric code such as a cylinder count is quantitative by this rule. It gets a continuous color scale and gradient legend unless you mark it as categorical. Field shorthand sets the type explicitly with a suffix: :Q (quantitative), :N (nominal), :O (ordinal), or :T (temporal). factor('cyl') is the equivalent of R’s factor(cyl), and its levels: argument sets the order.
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

use function Phiz\factor;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mtcars())
    ->aes(x: 'wt', y: 'mpg', color: factor('cyl'), shape: 'am:N')
    ->point(size: 60)
    ->labs(color: 'Cylinders', shape: 'Manual');

URL data cannot be inspected in PHP, so phiz assumes quantitative positions and nominal groupings. Use shorthand types for anything else.

Field definitions
field() builds a Field with any Vega-Lite field-definition property, such as field('date', timeUnit: 'month', title: 'Month') or field('term', sort: ['b', 'a', 'c']). A raw array is also accepted for any aesthetic and is used as given.
Field names containing dots or brackets, such as R’s Sepal.Length, are escaped automatically. Vega-Lite would otherwise read them as nested access.

text:
Choosing where to compute
The two approaches suit different data:

Server-side summaries send only the summarized rows to the page. They suit large tables, database queries, and statistics that need PHP, such as model fits. Each interaction costs a Livewire round trip.
Browser-side linking sends the raw rows once and responds to every interaction immediately. It suits up to a few thousand rows. Large data covers what to do beyond that.

Both approaches can share a page. For example, a Livewire filter can choose the rows, and a brush can explore them in the browser.

title: Design and compatibility
text:
phiz does not draw graphics. It translates a ggplot2-style description into a Vega-Lite specification. Vega-Lite then resolves scales, lays out facets and legends, runs transforms, handles interaction, and renders to canvas or SVG. The PHP side stays small, and plots behave the same in the browser and in static export.
Statistics run as Vega-Lite transforms where Vega-Lite has them: bins, densities with the default bandwidth, aggregates, quantiles, and window functions. phiz computes a statistic in PHP when Vega-Lite has no equivalent, or when matching R needs it:

smooth() fits and their confidence bands (loess up to 3,000 rows, lm, quad, and poly)
violin densities, and the R bw.nrd0 bandwidth behind density(adjust:)
2D densities, contours, and filled contours
ellipse() and the summaries of summary()
hex(), and bin2d() and histogram() above Config::$serverRows rows

Intervals
errorbar(), linerange(), and pointrange() draw intervals from ymin to ymax. With xmin and xmax they are horizontal. position: 'dodge' places groups side by side, which the coefficient plots use to compare models.
use Phiz\Plot;

$estimates = [
    ['site' => 'North', 'mean' => 4.1, 'lower' => 3.2, 'upper' => 5.0],
    ['site' => 'East', 'mean' => 5.3, 'lower' => 4.6, 'upper' => 6.1],

    ['site' => 'West', 'mean' => 4.8, 'lower' => 4.2, 'upper' => 5.5],
];

$plot = Plot::of($estimates)
    ->aes(x: 'site', y: 'mean', ymin: 'lower', ymax: 'upper')
    ->errorbar(width: 10)
    ->point(size: 60)
    ->hline(4.5, linetype: 'dashed', color: '#888888')
    ->labs(x: null, y: 'Mean score (95% CI)');

use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'cty', y: 'hwy')
    ->point(alpha: 0.4)

Annotations
annotate() adds a layer from fixed values rather than data, as ggplot2’s annotate() does. It draws text, label, point, segment, rect, rule, pointrange, linerange, errorbar, or crossbar. Positions can be single values or lists, and -INF and INF reach the edges of the panel. Annotations ignore the plot’s mappings, keep its axis titles, and appear in every facet panel.
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'cty', y: 'hwy')
    ->annotate('rect', xmin: 15, xmax: 20, ymin: -INF, ymax: INF, fill: 'orange', alpha: 0.2)
    ->count(alpha: 0.6)
    ->annotate('segment', x: 30, y: 25, xend: 33.5, yend: 42.5, color: '#D62728')
    ->annotate('text', x: 30, y: 23, label: 'Most efficient', color: '#D62728')
    ->labs(x: 'City mpg', y: 'Highway mpg');

title: Coming from ggplot2
text:
Differences
These differences follow from Vega-Lite rendering the plot.

Sizes. Point size is an area in square pixels, as in Vega-Lite, rather than a diameter in millimeters. The default is 30. linewidth is in pixels.
Bins. bins: is a maximum, and Vega-Lite rounds the boundaries. Use binwidth: and boundary: for exact bins.
Limits. xlim() and ylim() zoom without removing data. ggplot2 removes the data outside the limits, which changes statistics computed from it.
Densities. The default bandwidth is Vega-Lite’s. adjust: multiplies R’s bw.nrd0, so adjust: 1 reproduces ggplot2’s default.
Smoothers. Loess, lm, quad, and poly fits and their confidence bands are computed in PHP and match R. Loess matches loess(surface = "direct"); ggplot2 interpolates the loess surface, which moves the curve slightly. Above 3,000 rows, loess falls back to Vega-Lite’s transform without a band, where ggplot2 switches to a GAM. There is no gam method.
Colors. Categorical colors come from Vega-Lite’s palette by default. theme('gray') switches to ggplot2’s hue_pal() colors, computed for the number of levels. scaleColor(values:) or scheme: sets them explicitly.
Panels. A discrete axis is 300 pixels by default, the same as a continuous axis, and grows by 20 pixels per level beyond 15 levels.
Violins. violin() draws each violin as a Vega-Lite trail, whose ends are rounded. There is no draw_quantiles option; layer a boxplot() instead.
Polar coordinates. coordPolar() draws bars, columns, and arcs. Vega-Lite has no polar form for lines, points, or areas, so radar charts are not available.
Not available. There is no sec_axis(), no geom_dotplot(), and no geom_quantile(). Use raw() or layer() for any Vega-Lite feature phiz does not wrap.

Other approaches

Summarize first. phplyr’s group_by() and summarize(), or a SQL GROUP BY, usually answers the question with far fewer rows. Dashboards with Livewire shows charts built from summaries.
Load from a URL. Data::url('/data/points.csv') lets the browser fetch the file, so the page itself stays small. The browser still holds every row, so this helps page size, not drawing speed.
Sample. Bin::sample() keeps a uniform random subset when a scatterplot of individual points matters more than exact counts.

title: Rendering
text:
toArray() returns the Vega-Lite specification and toJson() encodes it. Plots also implement JsonSerializable. The specification declares the Vega-Lite 6 schema.
Four escape hatches reach the parts of Vega-Lite that phiz does not wrap:

raw([...]) deep-merges arbitrary Vega-Lite into the top level. Nested objects merge, and lists and scalars replace.
transform(...) adds Vega-Lite transforms that run before every layer.
layer([...]) adds a raw Vega-Lite layer.
param() and select() add raw parameters.

text:
HTML
embed() returns a container element followed by the script tags, and html() returns a standalone page. Both pass vega-embed options, such as ['actions' => false] or ['renderer' => 'svg'].
The container carries the specification in a data-phiz attribute. A small loader script, about 100 lines, renders every such element with vega-embed. It renders them again when the attribute changes. The same markup therefore works in static pages, Blade views, and Livewire components.
The browser libraries are pinned:



Library
Version




vega
6.4.0


vega-lite
6.4.3


vega-embed
7.3.0



Assets chooses where they come from:
use Phiz\Assets;

$plot->embed(assets: Assets::cdn());                 // jsDelivr, with subresource integrity (the default)
$plot->embed(assets: Assets::local('/js/vega'));     // copies you serve: vega.min.js, vega-lite.min.js, vega-embed.min.js
$plot->html(assets: Assets::inline('/path/to/js'));  // embedded in the page, for offline files
$plot->embed(assets: Assets::none());                // your bundle already sets window.vegaEmbed
$plot->embed(assets: false);                         // just the container

title: Rendering
text:
Static export
svg(), png(), pdf(), and save() run the vl-convert command-line tool. It renders without a browser, which suits reports, email, and print. vl-convert bundles its own Vega-Lite, and phiz runs it with Vega-Lite 6.1. The test suite validates every specification against the Vega-Lite 6.1 schema, so the same specification renders in both places.
$plot->save('figure.svg');
$plot->save('figure.png', scale: 3);
file_put_contents('figure.pdf', $plot->pdf());
phiz finds the binary through the PHIZ_VL_CONVERT or VL_CONVERT environment variable, then PATH. Download it from the vl-convert releases. Version 1.9.0 is tested. If the binary is missing, phiz throws Phiz\Exceptions\VlConvertNotFound with these instructions. new Export(binary: ..., timeout: ..., fontDir: ...) sets the binary path, the timeout, and an extra font directory explicitly.

Installing vl-convert
vl-convert has no Homebrew formula or apt package. Each release ships a self-contained binary for macOS (osx-arm64, osx-64) and Linux (linux-64, linux-aarch64). The Linux binaries link only against glibc and zlib, so they run on a bare Ubuntu image with no fonts or other packages installed. On Ubuntu the install is:
curl -sSLo /tmp/vl-convert.zip https://github.com/vega/vl-convert/releases/download/v1.9.0/vl-convert_linux-64.zip
sudo unzip -j -o /tmp/vl-convert.zip bin/vl-convert -d /usr/local/bin
vl-convert --version
On macOS, download vl-convert_osx-arm64.zip from the same release and unzip it the same way. The macOS binary has only an ad hoc signature. A copy fetched with curl or gh release download is not quarantined and runs directly. If a browser download is quarantined, xattr -d com.apple.quarantine vl-convert clears the flag. Put the binary in a directory on PATH, or point PHIZ_VL_CONVERT at it.


Reproducible SVG
SVG output from a given specification is byte-for-byte identical between runs, except for charts that use jitter(). Jitter is computed with Vega’s unseeded random(), so a jittered chart changes on every render. It is also identical between macOS and Linux, between ARM and x86, and with or without system fonts installed. vl-convert measures sans-serif text with its bundled Liberation Sans, so the layout does not depend on the machine’s fonts. The SVG keeps its text as <text font-family="sans-serif"> elements, so the viewer’s browser chooses the font that is displayed.
Committed SVG files therefore change only when the specification, the vl-convert version, or the pinned Vega-Lite version changes. A theme that names a font other than sans-serif, or an export with fontDir:, makes text measurement depend on the fonts available to vl-convert. Pin the vl-convert version wherever committed figures are generated.

title: Statistics
text:
The statistics helpers build ordinary plots from model results, so their output can be restyled with any Plot method. They read the arrays that phit returns, from its extension or its PHP polyfill. Formula fits from Phit\fit_lm, fit_glm, fit_lmer, and fit_glmer name their coefficients in columns. Matrix fits from fit_ols and fit_logistic take a names: argument.
The fits on this page are saved as JSON in docs/examples/fits/, from the mtcars and mpg data. phit’s polyfill, version 0.3.0, reproduces each of them to within 1e-13, relative. The test suite refits them and checks the coefficients and covariance matrices to 1e-9.

title: Statistics
text:
Requirements and fit keys
The helpers need no extension to plot a fit array. Two operations build design rows from the fit’s formula with Phit\model_matrix(), which comes from the phit extension or its polyfill:

predictions for formula fits in effect_plot(), predictions(), and marginal_means(), unless design: is given
random-slope design columns in random_effects_plot(), when it rebuilds conditional variances from the data

Without either, these calls throw an InvalidArgumentException. Each helper reads these keys of the fit array:







Helper
Keys




coefplot()
coefficients, conf_int, std_errors and df_residual when level: recomputes the intervals, columns or names:, and link for the axis label


residual_plot(), qq_plot(), fitted_plot()
fitted and residuals


scale_location_plot()
fitted, residuals, and sigma, or df_residual to estimate it


effect_plot(), predictions(), marginal_means()
coefficients, covariance, formula, columns, response, link, df_residual, and retained_rows when rows were dropped


random_effects_plot()
random, with effects_cond_var or random_effects_cond_var when present
